name: can-uds-smoke
description: CAN FRAMED-shape pilot over the SHIPPED clients: virtual (--backend virtual) vs real (--backend socketcan --target vcan0). Proves virtual == real frame-for-frame on the captured pcap frames, AND that each UDS response frame is actually present (expect). Each UDS exchange is a `can send 7E0 <sf>` followed by a `can dump -c 1`; the persistent bridge FIFO makes send-then-dump deterministic (the 7E8 response injected between the two connections survives). SINGLE-FRAME ISO-TP ONLY: the request payload is the already-SF-wrapped 8-byte CAN data ([PCI][pdu] 0x00-padded), since `can send` is a generalist raw inject that carries no ISO-TP knowledge. The `expect` values are the response UDS PDUs (hex), decoded from the captured frames by the comparator. Seed is course-FIXED (11223344), so it is in diff scope on both sides. Covers: open session, request seed, privileged read denied pre-unlock (NRC 33), invalid key (NRC 35, state does not advance), unlock, privileged read served.
